display.title: Yud-Tes Kislev: The Maggid's Yahrzeit and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai's Ruling
display.summary_short: Why we write our name under 'LaShem HaAretz', and a Chassid's dream on the Maggid's yahrzeit in which Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai rules that the Alter Rebbe will go free.
display.summary_long: The storyteller explains that a Rebbe is the 'head of the Jewish people': like Moshe Rabbeinu, the leader of each generation channels life to every Jewish soul. In a story the Rebbe told, a woman in a coma woke when the Frierdiker Rebbe's name was whispered in her ear, because a person's name joins the soul to the body. He then gives four reasons the Rebbe gave for writing 'LaShem HaAretz u'Meloah' with our name in our siddur and other sefarim. The story: when the Alter Rebbe was taken away in a black wagon, a Chassid named Reb Moshe fainted and woke only when told the Rebbe was freed. He fasted every day with other Chassidim. On the night of Yud-Tes Kislev, the Maggid of Mezritch's yahrzeit, he dozed at a farbrengen and dreamed that Reb Menachem Mendel of Horodok showed him the Heavenly gathering: the Maggid wept for his imprisoned student, and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai came and ruled that the Alter Rebbe would go free. A week later, a letter confirmed it.
display.lesson: Our name connects our soul to Hashem and to the Rebbe; say Tehillim with joy and trust.
